subject.title: Support multiple gateway tokens for multi-user session isolation

question: Should OpenClaw add a native Gateway multi-token principal model for token-mode Control UI/WebChat users, and should it be unified with scoped-token work in #92367?
rationale: The request changes public gateway auth config, credential matching, caller identity, session isolation, scopes/authorization, and trusted-proxy/device-token interactions, so automation cannot choose the security boundary.

options.title: Design unified principals
options.body: Define one Gateway-owned principal model covering per-user token identity, scoped service tokens, SecretRefs, rotation/revocation, audit behavior, docs, and tests.

options.title: Narrow to user labels
options.body: Add token-to-user labeling and session isolation first, accepting that scoped credentials and service principals may need a later migration.

options.title: Keep external front layers
options.body: Decline native multi-token support for now and document trusted-proxy or Pinchy-style frontends as the supported shared-user pattern.

recommendation.title: Design unified principals
recommendation.body: Define one Gateway-owned principal model covering per-user token identity, scoped service tokens, SecretRefs, rotation/revocation, audit behavior, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across gateway auth, config, Control UI, and security docs touched by this design.
